Fashola stated this during an exclusive interview with Arise News on Friday, where he made a case for Tinubu’s re-election ahead of the 2027 general election.
The former Lagos State governor, who is currently the All Progressives Congress (APC) Southwest Zonal Coordinator for Stakeholders’ Mobilisation, said Nigerians should assess the ability of presidential candidates to work with others before entrusting them with power.
He noted that the three major political figures seeking the nation’s leadership had all emerged from the governorship system, including former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, who was a governor-elect but did not eventually assume office.
According to him, the continued loyalty of those who worked with Tinubu, even when he was out of office, distinguishes him from other political leaders.
“The three main political candidates today share one trait in common. They all started as governors. One of them didn’t take office, but he was already a governor-elect, Vice President Atiku Abubakar.
“Where are all the people who worked with them today? That’s a job reference question. Why is it only President Tinubu that has all those who worked with him, still with him? And they were with him for 16 years or so, out of office when he wasn’t a president.
“Very, very good answer to the question. It shows an ability to work with others,” he said.
Fashola argued that anyone seeking to govern Nigeria must demonstrate the ability to build and sustain relationships, particularly given the country’s diverse political and cultural composition.
He said political leaders should not abandon their parties and associates whenever disagreements or crises arise.
“If you are going to get entrusted with managing Nigeria’s diverse family, you must be able to work in a team. And you don’t just get up and jump away when there’s crisis in the fold.
“There was crisis in the APC. It didn’t leave the party. The others have left the parties that brought them to prominence. They’ve left the people who work closely with them.
“And so people who are going to make this choice must look at the kind of people they want, who are asking them to be entrusted with power,” he added.
The former governor further argued that Tinubu’s political coalition had expanded beyond his longstanding associates to include individuals who previously opposed him.
According to Fashola, the president’s ability to bring former political adversaries into his camp contributed to the APC’s growing control of state governments.
“Now, you know the other interesting part of this story, this angle? All the people who opposed Tinubu when he used to be called the last man standing, all of them are now working with him.
“Not just those who worked with him before. Those who opposed him are now working with him.
“That’s how he has built a coalition of 30 state governors from one state, from Lagos. And that is profound.
“Whether you like him or not, he is able to be trusted with Nigeria’s diversity. Even his opponents, his fiercest foes in political context now work with him. That is a big reference for the job he’s seeking,” Fashola said.
His comments come amid opposition allegations that the Tinubu administration is consolidating political power and plotting to establish a one-party state, following the APC’s growing dominance across the country.
